note: Every number plotted, with where it came from. The README cites this file so a reader can check the figure against the records instead of trusting the picture.

provenance.omni_map: bench/results/sourcemap-ingest-2026-09-21.json (time, median of 3 for 10k and 50k; memory for 50k) and bench/results/sourcemap-memory-2026-09-30.json (memory for the 12-source and 10k points)
provenance.wba_363mb: bench/results/stats-ingest-2026-09-03.json, 63,617 ms / 2,295 MB on the corrected 363 MB fixture - also quoted in docs/en/evidence.md §2b
provenance.wba_1gb: docs/en/evidence.md §2, 176.3 s / 1,437 MB - baseline session, same reference machine, not the same run as the 363 MB row
provenance.sme: bench/results/sme-baseline-2026-09-03.json. The 12-source row is the real preact build (252 ms / 31 MB, median of 3); 10k is a median of 3; 50k is a single 9.4-minute run, because three runs would have taken half an hour
provenance.targets: docs/en/benchmarks.md - B3 <= 5 s / <= 200 MB, B4 <= 15 s / <= 400 MB, B5 <= 1 s, B8 < 500 MB
provenance.figures: bench/harness/make-charts.py draws the SVG directly with the standard library, so the figures are a function of charts-data.json and nothing else. bench/harness/check-chart-scales.mjs checks that each bar's pixel length is proportional to its value.

light.note: two linear panels, wall clock and peak memory, each on its own scale; the bands mark how far each axis runs, so a bar a couple of pixels long reads as a small value rather than as a broken render

dark.note: two linear panels, wall clock and peak memory, each on its own scale; the bands mark how far each axis runs, so a bar a couple of pixels long reads as a small value rather than as a broken render

light.note: log-log, with the area between the two series tinted and every gap labelled with its own multiple, because the geometry of a log axis cannot draw a ratio of 2,690 as 2,690 times anything
